label: Pair-rich histories can retain a fixed two-step law and exclude longer patterns
paraphrase: For each fixed cutoff, the two constant suffixes admit either value at every future coordinate but not every adjacent pair. The four period-three suffixes a,b,a XOR b admit every adjacent pair while satisfying the fixed recurrence f(t+2)=f(t) XOR f(t+1) after the record. Their first two suffix values determine the whole admitted history. This selector excludes a three-true suffix prefix, hence lacks both finite-pattern and whole-suffix richness. These are complete mathematical control histories; no actual law, metaphysical admissibility or chance measure is assigned.
